source_evidence.description: Original individual-level analysis HTML, containing embedded R and rendered results.

claims.claim: State life-expectancy association, first adjusted model
claims.tolerance: Equality at the precision printed in the article; conventional rounding.
claims.cause: The state-model coefficient SE was truncated rather than rounded.
claims.rationale: The source gives .07849 in the original Pandoc output, which rounds to .08 rather than the article’s .07.
claims.second_labeller_rationale: Code output is 0.07849, which rounds to 0.08, so the printed 0.07 is wrong at printed precision. It is a truncation error with no inferential consequence.
claims.r10_slip_evidence: Source report identifies truncation: .07849 printed as .07.

claims.tolerance: Equality at the precision printed in the article; conventional rounding.
claims.cause: The printed intercept differs from the original rendered analysis output.
claims.rationale: The source reports an intercept of 5.28, rather than 5.25.
claims.second_labeller_rationale: Shipped output gives 5.28 (raw 5.27565). The printed 5.25 differs beyond rounding. The intercept is not the focal estimate.
claims.r10_slip_evidence: Source report lists the intercept 5.25 vs 5.28 among the table's typos.

claims.claim: Individual abortion attitudes: uncertainty in the intercept
claims.tolerance: Equality at the precision printed in the article; conventional rounding.
claims.cause: The printed intercept CI differs from the original rendered analysis output.
claims.second_labeller_rationale: Both bounds differ from shipped output by more than rounding.
claims.r10_slip_evidence: Source report contrasts [5.08, 5.43] with [5.11, 5.44] in the intercept-typo discussion; both endpoints within 1%.

claims.tolerance: Equality at the precision printed in the article; conventional rounding.
claims.cause: Negative signs were added to both bounds of the life-expectancy CI.
claims.rationale: The source identifies both negative signs as erroneous. Static inspection of the original rendered HTML at https://osf.io/download/8wpgv/ confirms 0.09–0.40, without running or altering an analysis.
claims.reference_evidence: Static inspection of the authors' rendered individual-level HTML https://osf.io/download/8wpgv/ (pinned in package.version_pin); original confidence-interval output. Corroborating human report: https://osf.io/download/6a8dab91bef1626ff08e0770/ — §2 Computational Reproducibility, pp. 4–5: “typos”.
claims.second_labeller_rationale: Code gives [0.09, 0.40]. The printed [−0.09, −0.40] has the wrong sign. The point estimate and p-value are printed correctly, so this is a sign typo on a printed number.

claims.tolerance: Equality at the precision printed in the article; conventional rounding.
claims.cause: A negative sign was added to the lower income-group CI bound.
claims.rationale: The source identifies the lower-bound negative sign as erroneous. Static inspection of the original rendered HTML at https://osf.io/download/8wpgv/ confirms 0.03–0.36.
claims.reference_evidence: Static inspection of the authors' rendered individual-level HTML https://osf.io/download/8wpgv/ (pinned in package.version_pin); original confidence-interval output. Corroborating human report: https://osf.io/download/6a8dab91bef1626ff08e0770/ — §2 Computational Reproducibility, pp. 4–5: “typos”.
claims.second_labeller_rationale: Code gives [0.03, 0.36], which excludes zero and is consistent with p = .023. The printed lower bound has the wrong sign. This is a control variable.

claims.claim: Individual abortion attitudes: life-expectancy point estimate
claims.tolerance: Equality at the precision printed in the article; conventional rounding.
claims.rationale: The source assesses this result using the original analysis and reports reproduction at the article’s precision.
claims.second_labeller_rationale: The main individual-level estimate reproduces exactly at printed precision.

notes.sol: Original R is embedded in the public HTML. The source reconstructs an analysis dataset using the embedded original preprocessing code because one preprocessed spreadsheet has misnamed columns. Imputation changes, new control variables and newer life-expectancy data are excluded.
notes.claude: C1 and C4 are P2 under R2. No paper alternative under R7. The input files are now pinned. Reconciled with the second labeller (see reconciliation.md). The final judgement is the structured label; notes_blind_original keeps the pre-reconciliation blind notes, which are historical and superseded wherever they conflict with the final label.
notes.claude_blind_original_historical: The package has no R scripts. Code is embedded in rendered HTML (R Markdown output), and values were checked against that output. The report notes that the preprocessed individual-level xlsx has misnamed columns that cause an error when subsetting. The reproducers bypassed this by rebuilding the data from the code, so it was not a blocker for the numbers. The report calls the paper reproducible 'with the exception of a few minor typos'. Under the ReproCrowd rule the printed numbers differ from the code output, so I labelled them discrepant and the paper 'computational issues'. 'Computationally reproducible' is an acceptable alternative if the reconciler treats printed typos against correct code output as reporting rather than computational issues. C1: 'close' is a defensible alternative (truncation, difference < 0.01). C4 severity: P1 is arguable, since this is the CI of the focal predictor on the primary DV. I chose P2 because the estimate and p-value are correct and the error is an obvious sign typo. Supplement issues (Table S-4 infant mortality 0.45/2.75 vs code 0.41/2.58; S-6 analysis absent) are outside the claim list. Pin completeness: the version pin lists codebooks, raw-data zips and HTML outputs only. The preprocessed data the report refers to sit in OSF folders ('1 State-level data', '2 Individual-level data', '3 Nation-level data') that are not pinned.
